title: cs-public0

list.name: instance
list.label: Instance
list.description: Choose one or more monitored exporter instances, or All to view them together.

panels.title: Known telemetry
panels.description: 1 means the required telemetry checks completed successfully for the latest sample; 0 means the observations are missing or unreliable. A known sample does not prove complete inspection or absence of fail-open bypass.

panels.title: Sensor running
panels.description: 1 means the expected Suricata sensor process is running and matches the monitored identity; 0 means this check did not succeed. A running process alone does not prove packet inspection or forwarding health. Read this together with Known telemetry.

panels.title: Queue listener
panels.description: 1 means the monitored NFQUEUE has a userspace listener; 0 means the expected listener is absent. Listener presence alone does not prove that every selected packet reaches Suricata or is inspected.

panels.title: Selector installed
panels.description: 1 means the expected cs-public0 nftables queue selector was found for the configured bridge and queue; 0 means the check did not succeed. This verifies the selector's presence, not complete network coverage.

panels.title: Degraded latch
panels.description: 1 is the latched history of observed degradation, such as counter increases, resets or sensor restarts. The latch can remain set after the current sample recovers. A clear latch does not rule out unmeasured loss or fail-open bypass.

panels.title: Publication age
panels.description: Seconds since the last telemetry publication, calculated from the publication timestamp. A rising age means the publisher or scrape path may be stale. Missing data is Unknown, not a fresh publication.

panels.title: Queue pending
panels.description: Packets currently waiting in the monitored NFQUEUE. Sustained growth suggests the userspace consumer is not keeping up. An empty queue alone does not prove complete inspection or absence of bypass.

panels.title: Packets selected by nftables per second
panels.description: Five-minute rate of packets selected at the nftables hook. Full-queue fail-open packets can increment this counter without receiving an NFQUEUE ID. This is not the number enqueued or completely inspected.

panels.title: Engine decoded packets per second
panels.description: Five-minute rate of packets reported by Suricata's decoder. It is an engine counter, not a count of unique requests or confirmed attacks. Offload and sampling boundaries can make it differ from the nftables rate.

panels.title: Queue drops
panels.description: Sum of the kernel and userspace NFQUEUE drop counters. These are queue delivery losses, not packets blocked by an IPS signature. Zero does not prove complete inspection: some fail-open paths do not increment these counters.

panels.title: Netlink socket drops per second
panels.description: Lost netlink messages for the monitored socket. Separate from kernel/user queue losses and rule-driven IPS drops. Zero cannot exclude full-queue fail-open. Missing or stale publications remain Unknown. Freshness is matched on instance, bridge and queue: runtime/cs_public0.py publish_metrics emits bridge and queue on every metric, including last_publish_unix_seconds; Prometheus supplies instance.

panels.title: Accounting gap: nft versus NFQUEUE IDs
panels.description: Observed discrepancy between nft selection and NFQUEUE IDs. It is not an HTTP request count or a direct count of confirmed fail-open packets. A positive gap remains visible even when combined telemetry is unknown. Missing or stale publications remain Unknown. Freshness is matched on instance, bridge and queue: runtime/cs_public0.py publish_metrics emits bridge and queue on every metric, including last_publish_unix_seconds; Prometheus supplies instance.

description: Operational health of cs-public0 bridge inspection. Select one or more instances to inspect telemetry, the sensor, NFQUEUE and packet counters. These are health observations, not an attack verdict or proof of complete inspection. Missing values mean Unknown. Use the separate optional Wazuh dashboard for alert signatures and source IPs.
